status: Pilot, written by Claude on 12 November 2026 and not yet checked by the translation workers. Each lesson's description is its teaching note until the lesson board exists.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Letter Ñ, Part 1
lessons.description: Ñ is its own letter in Spanish, said like the "ny" in canyon. Listen for it in año, niño, mañana, and España.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Rolled R, Part 1
lessons.description: One R is a quick tap; two are rolled, and the difference changes the word. Hear pero against perro, and caro against carro.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - The Silent H, Part 1
lessons.description: The letter H is written in Spanish and never said. Listen to hola, ahora, huevo, and hoy.

lessons.title: Sounds and Script - Accent Marks, Part 1
lessons.description: An accent mark can be the only thing that tells two words apart. Compare sí with si, and tú with tu.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb ir, to go, changes to say who is going. Spot what changes: voy, vas, va, vamos.

lessons.title: Patterns - To Go in the Present, Part 2
lessons.description: More of ir, to go: for all of you, for them, for "let's", and for what you are about to do.

lessons.title: Patterns - More Than One, Part 1
lessons.description: For more than one, the word gains an S, and so does its "the": el becomes los, and la becomes las.

lessons.title: Patterns - Words That Match, Part 1
lessons.description: A describing word matches the thing it describes: rojo with el carro, roja with la casa. Spot the ending that changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Asking a Question, Part 1
lessons.description: A Spanish question opens with ¿ and closes with ?. Often the words barely move, and the voice rises instead.
words: This is the bus to Barcelona.
Este es el autobús a Barcelona.
Is this the bus to Barcelona?

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Saying No, Part 1
lessons.description: To say something is not so, put no in front of the verb. Nothing else in the sentence changes.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Describing Words Come After, Part 1
lessons.description: In English the describing word comes first: a white house. In Spanish it usually comes after: una casa blanca.

lessons.title: Sentence Building - Leaving Out I and You, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb's ending already says who is doing it, so Spanish usually leaves out I, you, we, and they.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Going Places, Part 1
lessons.description: The verb ir, to go, at work in whole sentences. Spot voy, vamos, vas, and van.
words: I am going to the market.
We are going to the beach.
Are you going to the party?

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Questions and Answers, Part 1
lessons.description: A question and its answer, side by side. Spot what the answer keeps from the question, and what it changes.
words: No, I do not speak English.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Describing Things, Part 1
lessons.description: Describing words matching what they describe, in whole sentences: blanca, rojos, alta, pequeños.

lessons.title: Sentences in Use - Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, Part 1
lessons.description: One trip to the market, told three ways: already done, happening now, and still to come.
words: I went to the market yesterday.
I am going to the market today.
I will go to the market tomorrow.
I am going to go tomorrow.
